clue.text: Sort of case for Alfred's common seal

indicators.note: a sort of case is a variant of it, so the four letters of case are reworked

parts.note: Alf is the familiar short form of the name Alfred

explanation.surface: Someone describes a type of box or container belonging to a man called Alfred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' turns CASE into SEAC; add ALF, short for Alfred, and 'for' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea calf is an old popular name for the harbour or common seal of northern coasts.

clue.text: Large bag for plunder

definitions.meaning: a big coarse bag for coal or potatoes
to loot or pillage a captured town

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a big coarse bag, and the verb for pillaging a captured town.

clue.text: The "watch chain" French knight, star of the old music halls

definitions.text: star of the old music halls

parts.note: an albert is a heavy chain for a pocket watch, named after Prince Albert
chevalier is the French word for a knight or horseman

explanation.surface: A music-hall performer is introduced by a nickname and a French title.
explanation.walkthrough: An ALBERT is a Victorian pocket-watch chain. Music halls were Britain's popular variety theatres of the 19th and early 20th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Chevalier was a celebrated Victorian music-hall comedian and singer, known for coster songs.

clue.text: Consented to take old soldier in

indicators.note: to take something in is to enclose it, so one piece wraps round another
completes the phrase take in, signalling that one piece holds the other

parts.note: someone old is aged
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to give a veteran a place to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' and 'in' together form the container signal. 'old soldier' looks like one unit, a veteran, but it splits into two pieces; RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To have consented is to have agreed: both mean said yes to a proposal.

clue.text: Sets Cockney senses tingling with superfluous ornaments

indicators.note: London Cockney speech turns a th sound into f, so the th is replaced

parts.note: tingling sensations of excitement are thrills

explanation.surface: Fancy decorations make someone's senses tingle in a London accent.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney says 'frills' for THRILLS, swapping TH for F. Cockney is the working-class accent of East London. 'Sets' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Frills are unnecessary decorative extras, from the ruffled edging on clothes.

clue.text: Everyone in feud unusually mature

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as the clue says everyone is in it
the letters of feud appear in an unusual order

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: The whole company is embroiled in a strange quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' gives FDUE, the scrambled feud, and 'in' places everyone inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill or bond that matures becomes payable, which is what falling due means.

clue.text: Jack Sprat's wife was one with an overweight boyfriend

definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme she could eat no lean, so she liked fatty meat
a woman whose partner is fat has a corpulent sweetheart

explanation.definitionFit: Read one way it means someone fond of fat; read another, a lover who is fat.

clue.text: Deceives over accommodation, so keeps a low profile

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits over, above, the other

parts.note: someone who deceives lies
a flat is a set of rooms to live in

explanation.surface: Someone lies about their living arrangements and keeps their head down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts LIES above FLAT in this down entry; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying flat is an idiom for staying out of sight and avoiding attention.

clue.text: Make inferences from tie ends

parts.note: a tied match is a draw
endings are conclusions

explanation.surface: Someone deduces things from the loose ends of a necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' looks like the neckwear but is a drawn game; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw conclusions is the idiom for reasoning from evidence to an inference.

clue.text: Undertaking that requires initiative

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a venture taken on and the go-getting spirit needed for one.

clue.text: Pole having to live in vehicle

indicators.note: the clue places one piece inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Someone has to live in their car with a long pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is only a link; 'in' is the container signal, putting living inside the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is the tree-trunk pole tossed in Scottish Highland games.

clue.text: Curious hatpin set of some time ago

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters are set in an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd set of hatpins is described as an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' rearranges HATPIN and SET together; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done some time ago happened in former days, an idiom for formerly.

clue.text: Quiet policeman, for instance, who can deal with any complaints

definitions.text: who can deal with any complaints

parts.note: quiet and well-behaved means orderly
a policeman is an example of an officer

explanation.surface: A calm police officer is the one to handle grievances.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British Army the orderly officer is the officer on duty for the day, who hears soldiers' complaints at meals and inspections.
explanation.definitionFit: The duty officer of the day in a regiment is the one who receives and handles complaints.

clue.text: Hellish place to be when put out of joint?

parts.note: Dis is the underworld, the city of hell in Dante
to be somewhere is to be located there

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether being in hell is what it means to have a dislocated limb.
explanation.walkthrough: DIS, the classical underworld, plus LOCATED: located in Dis. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dislocated bone has been forced out of its joint.

clue.text: Island of a certain charm

indicators.note: the answer is formed of letters from the words that follow

explanation.surface: An island is said to have a certain charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' marks the letters inside certaIN CHarm. Inch is Scottish for a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch, from Gaelic innis, is a small island in Scottish place names.

clue.text: One who hangs on to a fee

definitions.meaning: a servant or follower kept on in a household for years
an advance payment that secures someone's services

explanation.definitionFit: A family servant kept for years and a fee securing a lawyer are both called this.

clue.text: Produce something from the bicycle shed?

definitions.text: Produce something from the bicycle shed?

parts.words: Produce something from the bicycle shed?
parts.note: to produce an idea or person again is to trot it out; bringing bikes out of a shed means rolling them on their wheels

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to bring out a familiar thing or person, literally to roll it out.

clue.text: Believe number's up in Devon

parts.note: to credit a story is to believe it

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: no. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Someone believes that their number is up somewhere in Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the abbreviation for number in this down entry. Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crediton is a small market town north-west of Exeter in Devon, so it is a place in that county.

clue.text: General with unruly horse in a dangerous situation

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general

indicators.note: an unruly horse is out of control, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A general on a wild horse finds himself in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: LEE plus HORSE rearranged as SHORE by 'unruly'. 'with' and 'in' are links. General Lee famously rode a horse, Traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: A lee shore, with the wind blowing a ship onto it, is a classic peril for sailing vessels.

clue.text: Unhappy to hear it's a girl

indicators.note: the clue asks us to listen, so the sound of the words matters

parts.note: a girl is a lass

explanation.surface: A parent is unhappy to learn the baby is a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hear' says 'a lass' sounds like the exclamation; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection expresses sorrow or regret, the cry of someone unhappy.

clue.text: Marksman who fires at bird (rook)

parts.note: the snipe is a wading bird
R is the chess notation for a rook

explanation.surface: A marksman shoots at a bird, which turns out to be a rook.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb snipe comes from shooting snipe, a hard bird to hit. 'who fires at' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a skilled marksman who shoots from hiding.

clue.text: Stumble when going up for examinations

parts.note: to stumble is to trip

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means read from the bottom

parts.note: so can mean then or in that case, standing for when

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on the way up to sit their exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' reverses the second piece in this down entry. Going up is also British for starting university, which suits the Cambridge exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tripos is the set of final honours examinations at Cambridge University.

clue.text: Publishing house introducing historian to journalists

indicators.note: the historian comes first, leading in the journalists

parts.note: Edward Hyde, Earl of Clarendon, wrote the History of the Rebellion
the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: A historian is introduced to a group of reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Clarendon Press, Oxford University Press's imprint, was funded partly by profits from Clarendon's History.
explanation.definitionFit: The Clarendon Press is the Oxford University imprint, a long-established publishing house.

clue.text: Observe student lifting the dregs

indicators.note: in a down entry lifting raises the letters, reading them upward

parts.note: to observe is to see
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Someone watches a student hoisting the leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns SEE + L, SEEL, upward to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the sediment at the bottom of wine, the dregs.

clue.text: Hint of pot design without an adequate cover

indicators.note: a design is an arrangement, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: the fodder words as printed; the setter needs 'Hint on pot'

explanation.surface: A trace of a pot's pattern lacks a proper lid.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed 'Hint of pot' has an F where a second N is needed; with 'on' for 'of' the letters rearrange exactly into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bald leaves the head without proper covering of hair, a jocular idiom for balding.

clue.text: Turn out to be soft over accident

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: by accident the letters fall into a different order

explanation.surface: A soft landing turns out to follow an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: P, then OVER rearranged as ROVE by 'accident'.
explanation.definitionFit: To prove to be something is to turn out that way in the end.

clue.text: What overzealous sun worshipper gets in the shade

definitions.meaning: someone who sunbathes too much ends up deeply bronzed

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the result of too much sunbathing and a deep brown colour.

clue.text: Opposes one in stress, perhaps

indicators.note: the clue puts one inside the other piece
perhaps hints the letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone resists an emphasis on stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges STRESS, and 'in' puts I inside: RES-I-STS.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist something is to oppose it or stand against it.
